title: add-econ-starter-profiles-and-safe-fallthrough-logic
author: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Introduce a small, opinionated set of 'econ starter' presets (batching, cache, and quantization defaults) plus a runtime-safe fallthrough policy that selects conservative execution profiles when a new workload is unseen or when model variants fail. Motivation: Many teams waste cycles tuning cost controls on day one. We provide reasonable, production-minded defaults that reduce token cost and risk while allowing teams to opt into aggressive profiles later. Design: - econ starter presets: small/medium/large workload presets capturing batch size, prefix cache TTL, and a quantization hint (fp16/int8-lite) tuned for latency-sensitive and cost-sensitive shapes. Each preset includes minimum safety bounds (max latency, fallback thresholds). - safe fallthrough policy: runtime policy that, when a request hits an unknown route or when a selected profile fails runtime constraints (latency SLO or memory OOM), automatically falls back to the next conservative preset and records a structured event. - warm-start seeding: when a new route is created, the controller seeds the route with the best-fit starter based on historical token-length histogram if available, otherwise uses 'small' preset. - telemetry and eval hooks: add unit-econ tags and a lightweight evaluation hook to run quick microbenchmarks during canary to estimate per-token cost impact. Rollout: canary on 10% of routes for 48h, automatic rollback triggers on cost regressions > 15% or latency p95 increase > 20%. Checklist: - [x] starter presets defined and documented - [x] runtime fallthrough implemented - [x] metrics emitted for fallback_count and seed_reason - [x] unit and integration tests - [x] docs + console dropdown for starter selection - [x] canary rollout plan in release notes Related: linear ENG-2109, PM-121, support SUP-3421. Jira: INT-712 (follow-up for extended quant profiles). Notes: kept conservative defaults intentionally to avoid large unit-econ regressions on first-use. This description contains design rationale, telemetry, and rollout guidance inlined to help reviewers evaluate safety implications.
